title: 7 Things to Compare Before You Pick a Shilajit Format
meta_description: Resin, capsules, gummies: what the human trials actually tested, what moved, and the one thing no study has measured yet.

hero.title: to Compare Before a Shilajit Format
hero.summary_html: Summary: Resin, capsules, and gummies are tested very differently. Here is what each form's trials actually measured.

items.title: Three formats, three methods
items.body:
Shilajit is sold as a raw resin you pinch into water, a capsule with a standardized extract inside, or a gummy with shilajit added to a sweetened base.

Each format changes how much fulvic acid and trace mineral content actually reaches the dose, not just how it tastes.
items.evidence: Product category overview, no clinical claim
items.alt: A pinch of dark resin, a capsule, and a gummy laid out on travertine stone

items.title: Capsule trial raised testosterone
items.body:
In a placebo-controlled trial of men aged 45 to 55, a purified shilajit capsule taken twice daily for 90 days raised free testosterone 19.14 percent versus baseline.

DHEAS, a related hormone, rose 31.35 percent over the same 90 days. Placebo did not match either change.

chart.title: Change vs baseline, day 90
chart.source: Pandit S et al. Andrologia 2016;48(5):570-575. 75 men aged 45 to 55, 90 days, purified shilajit capsule vs placebo, randomised double-blind.

items.evidence_label: Human RCT · Pandit et al., Andrologia 2016

items.title: No trial tested shilajit gummies
items.body:
We searched Europe PMC and PubMed for a human trial of a shilajit gummy. We found none.

Gummy formulas also carry less active material per serving than a resin or a standardized capsule, since sugar and gelling agents take up space in the dose.
items.evidence: Evidence gap: Europe PMC and PubMed search 2026-10-12, no shilajit gummy trial found
items.alt: Printed research papers and reading glasses beside an empty gummy dish on linen
items.evidence_label: Literature check · no gummy trial found

items.title: Resin pilot had no placebo
items.body:
A 28-day pilot study gave 25 healthy men a daily dose of shilajit resin (exact amount in the chart source below). Leg press strength rose 12.94 percent and grip strength rose 5.73 percent.

The design was open label with no placebo arm, so some of that gain could reflect training familiarity rather than the resin alone.

chart.title: 28-day open-label pilot, 25 men
chart.source: Yadav D et al. Cureus 2026;18(1):e102372. 25 healthy men, 28 days, 500 mg/day TruBlk shilajit resin, open-label single-arm pilot.

items.evidence_label: Open-label pilot · Yadav et al., Cureus 2026

items.title: Trials measured different things
items.body:
The capsule trial measured hormone levels in blood. The resin pilot measured strength and endurance in the gym. Neither trial measured the other's outcome.

That makes format-to-format comparison a guess dressed up as a fact. Read what a study measured before you read what it means.
items.evidence: Study design comparison, no new claim
items.alt: Two open notebooks with different handwritten charts on a stone desk

items.title: Contamination risk, any format
items.body:
A 2025 lab survey tested raw shilajit and finished shilajit supplements for thallium, a toxic metal. Trace amounts turned up in both, and the exact levels are in the chart source below.

Some finished products tested higher than the raw material they came from. The survey did not break results out by resin versus capsule versus gummy.
items.alt: A gloved hand holding lab test strips over a petri dish, no face visible
items.evidence_label: Lab survey · Kamgar et al., BMC Chemistry 2025

items.title: Ask for third-party lab tests
items.body:
Since the contamination study above found no safe format, the only control left is testing. Ask a brand for a current batch's heavy-metal lab result before you buy.

A brand that will not produce one is a bigger red flag than the format you pick.
items.evidence: Buying guidance drawn from the lab survey above
items.alt: A printed lab certificate of analysis on a travertine desk beside a pen

bridge.title: What the label on this jar actually says
bridge.body:
Pure Shilajit Gold Resin is the raw-resin format above: no capsule shell, no gummy base. The jar's own label states 75% Fulvic Acid, with the full weight and serving count printed on the product page.

That is what the label prints. It is not a restatement of either trial above, since neither trial tested this exact product.

Taking medication or managing a health condition? Check with a doctor first.
